item: A signed key-rotation record lets the custody log verify across a change of key
key_paths: src/custody/log.py; src/custody/signing.py; src/api/custody.py; src/static/app-ai-tools.js; scripts/verify_custody.py; tests/test_custody_key_rotation.py
summary: When the key that signs now did not sign the tail, the log writes a key-rotation record first, signed by the new key and saying in plain words that the previous key was not available. CustodyLog.rotate_signing_key writes an endorsed one: the old key signs the new key and the chain position. The checker follows an endorsed rotation and names it; refuses an unendorsed one unless accept_unendorsed_rotation (--accept-unendorsed-rotation) is passed; and refuses a key change with no record, so a forged tail stays refused. One-item exports carry every rotation record. An export after a key change records the rotation before the new key signs its head; a long-lived log reloads its signer when the key file changes rather than rotating back and forth; the in-app check follows the key too; a verified bundle names its line of keys; the CLI refuses an unknown option.
